Definition: from G571; faithlessness, i.e. (negatively) disbelief (lack of Christian faith), or (positively) unfaithfulness (disobedience):--unbelief.
BiblicalUsage: Unbelief, and Jesus meets it everywhere. He marvelled because of their unbelief in His own country in Mark 6:6, and did not many mighty works there because of their unbelief in Matthew 13:58. The father in Mark 9:24 shows the other face of it — ‘Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief’ — and Paul gives the warning in Romans 11:20: the branches were broken off because of unbelief, and thou standest by faith; be not highminded, but fear.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that unbelief is not the absence of evidence but the refusal to trust what is in front of us. The father who cried for help against his own unbelief was heard, while the crowds who settled into theirs saw few mighty works. Fear, not pride, is the right posture — I stand by faith, and faith is a gift I did not earn.
